text:
maria: Heads-up — canary 2026.3 rolled at 18:05, seeing an error spike on the embeddings route, ~0.9% 5m error rate and p95 +180ms. Suggest we consider manual rollback if this doesn't stabilize. :eyes:

deploy-bot: [ALERT] canary-2026.3 health degraded. error_rate=0.93% (threshold=0.5%). recent logs: https://logs.prod/redwood/2026.3/embed :warning:

leo: Do we have stack traces or a dominant error class? Any customer-facing failures yet?

maria: ~120 req/min to embeddings, ~15 failing/min, mostly 500s from runtime kv-cache miss + inconsistent key hash. No large customer hits reported but trend is rising.

jamal: Proposal: immediate traffic pin back to stable variant on canary hosts and then do a manual rollback. Automated rollback threshold should remain as fallback (>=1.5% sustained for 2m). Manual now since we see correlated 500s from the same signature.

sre-oncall: +1. Action checklist:
- leo: perform traffic pin on edge/router
- jamal: prepare rollback command and smoke tests
- maria: pre-write customer comms for #prod-status and release notes

leo: Executing pin: `rwctl route update canary --to model:2026.2 --weight 100` (running)

deploy-bot: Routing change accepted. rolling out config to 6 canary hosts. ETA ~30s.

leo: Routing change complete. Observing metrics... p95 and error rate trending down within 45s.

maria: Drafting comms: "We briefly routed canary traffic away from the new variant due to elevated 500s; traffic is back on the stable model while we investigate. No customer action required."

jamal: Rollback command ready if needed: ```sh
deploy rollback --target model:2026.2 --mode manual --reason "kv-cache mismatch in 2026.3"
``` Run smoke: `curl -sS https://canary.api/redwood/embed | jq .status`

sre-oncall: Also recording follow-ups: add KV cache warmup to rollout checklist, add auto-pin threshold at 0.8% for canary routes, and add a brief preflight that checks key-hash consistency between builds.

maria: I'll file a short post with logs and link to the runbook changes. If we see re-escalation we'll open an incident. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
